key_insight: The paper introduces a Multi-block-Single-probe Variance Reduction (MSVR) estimator that can track many coupled component functions efficiently even when only a few stochastic blocks are observable per iteration.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster and more sample-efficient optimization for finite-sum coupled compositional problems that appear in large-scale machine learning and multi-task learning systems.
method: Use partial block sampling to update an estimator of the full coupled vector g(w) with only O(1) block probes per step.
Build optimization algorithms on top of MSVR for non-convex, convex, strongly convex, and PL settings.
Exploit linear outer gradients to further improve the dependence on m.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved sample complexity across multiple objective classes and empirical gains on multi-task deep AUC maximization.
watch_item: Performance and stability may depend on the quality of stochastic oracles and the choice of block sampling strategy, especially in large m settings.
paper_title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator
